title: 'Maybank, Asian Banking School Explore Certification Programme For Wealth Advisory
text:
'Maybank, Asian Banking School Explore Certification Programme For Wealth Advisory

'Maybank and the Asian Banking School (ABS) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to explore the development of a professional certification framework for wealth advisory in Malaysia, aimed at introducing an industry-recognised benchmark for advisory capability.  The proposed certification framework, to be known as the ABS Wealth Advisory & Management Certification Programme, is intended to establish competency standards specifically for wealth advisory professionals in banking. Upon its launch, it will be Malaysia’s first industry-wide professional certification framework dedicated to wealth advisory.  The parties noted that as wealth management needs grow more complex, clients increasingly require advice that connects different aspects of their financial lives. This initiative they added aims to establish a consistent benchmark for the advisory capabilities required to serve clients holistically.  Maybank will serve as the Founding Industry Partner, contributing insights and its experience in developing wealth talent, while ABS will bring its expertise in professional banking development and certification. ABS will retain independence over the standards and how they are assessed and certified.  “This collaboration with the Asian Banking School allows us to contribute that experience beyond our organisation, to raise professional standards for wealth advisory in Malaysia, with the opportunity to extend elements of the programme across the region over time,” said Syed Ahmad Taufik Albar, Group CEO, Community Financial Services, Maybank.  The programme’s first intake is expected in the second half of 2027, and Maybank intends to incorporate the programme into Maybank Wealth Academy, connecting it with structured learning and career development through practical workplace application. The parties will also explore opportunities to extend relevant certification pathways to wealth professionals across the region.

title: 'Equal work, equal pay
text:
'Equal work, equal pay

'I guess Lim Guan Eng, the former finance minister and now adviser to the Democratic Action Party (DAP), has a soft spot for employers. His call to exclude migrant workers from the minimum wage and the paltry 2% contribution to the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) repeats a position he took in early August 2025. Even then, labour groups criticised it. Since he has chosen to lend his voice to employers, be they micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) or others, it is apt to remind him of three fundamental issues. All people are equal Article 8(1) of the Federal Constitution treats everyone as equal and entitles them to equal protection. The courts have noted this. In Ahmad Zahri bin Mirza Abdul Hamid v AIMS Cyberjaya Sdn Bhd, the Federal Court took cognisance of Article 10 of the International Labour Organization (ILO) Migrant Workers (Supplementary Provisions) Convention 143 of 1975. It said Malaysia should promote and guarantee equality of opportunity and treatment between migrant workers and nationals. This is also consonant with Article 8(1) of the Federal Constitution which essentially provides that all persons are equal before the law and entitled to the equal protection of the law. his judgment alone should put to rest the flawed argument that Malaysia should adopt discriminatory standards against migrant workers to protect employers. Legislative protection Section 69F of the Employment Act 1955 empowers the director general of labour to inquire into and decide any dispute over discrimination in employment. An employer who fails to comply with the director general’s order faces, on conviction, a fine of up to RM50,000. For a continuing offence, there is a further fine of up to RM1,000 for each day it continues. Where an employer has signed a collective agreement with a trade union, section 17(1)(b) of the Industrial Relations Act 1967 makes it binding once the Industrial Court takes cognisance of it. It covers all worker employed in the undertaking, now or later. Industrial Court and other judicial decisions have affirmed that such agreements apply to migrant workers. International standards From the Universal Declaration of Human Rights to the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR) and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, one fact stands unchallenged – there is no room for discriminatory employment practices against migrant workers.

title: 'AHB kekalkan agihan pendapatan 5.00 sen seunit, pemegang unit terima RM236.41 juta bagi FY2026 | DagangNews - Berita Bisnes Anda
text:
'AHB kekalkan agihan pendapatan 5.00 sen seunit, pemegang unit terima RM236.41 juta bagi FY2026 | DagangNews - Berita Bisnes Anda

'KUALA LUMPUR 1 Okt - Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera (AHB) mengekalkan jumlah agihan pendapatan termasuk bonus sebanyak 5.00 sen seunit bagi tahun kewangan berakhir 30 September 2026 (FY2026), dengan keseluruhan pembayaran RM236.41 juta yang memberi manfaat kepada lebih 82,000 pemegang unit. Pelaburan Hartanah Berhad (PHB) bersama pengurus dananya, PHB Asset Management Berhad (PHBAM), mengumumkan agihan pendapatan akhir sebanyak 2.10 sen seunit bagi tempoh enam bulan berakhir 30 September 2026, menurut kenyataan PHB bersama hari ini. PHB selaku penaja dana turut mengisytiharkan edaran bonus sebanyak 0.40 sen seunit, menjadikan jumlah agihan bagi tempoh tersebut sebanyak 2.50 sen seunit. Bonus itu diberikan kepada pegangan sehingga satu juta unit pertama bagi setiap pemegang unit. Selepas mengambil kira agihan pendapatan interim sebanyak 2.50 sen seunit yang diumumkan pada April 2026, jumlah agihan bagi FY2026 mencapai 5.00 sen seunit. Agihan akhir itu membabitkan pembayaran RM120.13 juta. Agihan pendapatan tersebut adalah bersih selepas cukai dan zakat, membolehkan pemegang unit menerima jumlah penuh tanpa sebarang potongan atau tanggungan tambahan. Pembayaran akan dibuat dalam bentuk unit AHB dan dikreditkan terus ke dalam akaun pemegang unit selewat-lewatnya pada 13 Oktober 2026. Pengarah Urusan Kumpulan PHB, Mazuki Abdullah @ Muhammad berkata agihan bagi FY2026 mencerminkan ketahanan berterusan AHB dan kekuatan portfolio hartanahnya, disokong pendekatan pengurusan aset serta pelaburan yang berdisiplin. “Prestasi AHB pada tahun ini membuktikan komitmen kami untuk terus memberikan pulangan yang kompetitif kepada pemegang unit,” katanya. Beliau berkata PHB terus memperkukuh kedudukan AHB sebagai instrumen pelaburan pilihan pelabur Bumiputera melalui pengurusan modal yang berhemat, strategi pelaburan dinamik dan pengoptimuman portfolio bagi memastikan pertumbuhan mampan serta penciptaan nilai jangka panjang. Menurut Mazuki, penawaran tambahan sebanyak 400 juta unit AHB yang diumumkan baru-baru ini memperluas peluang kepada lebih ramai pelabur Bumiputera untuk mengambil bahagian dalam pelaburan hartanah komersial utama. Beliau berkata AHB akan terus menyokong pembentukan kekayaan jangka panjang Bumiputera dan menjana nilai mampan kepada pemegang unit. Komitmen itu selaras dengan aspirasi Pelan Transformasi Ekonomi Bumiputera 2035 (PUTERA35) untuk memperkukuh penyertaan ekonomi, pemilikan dan pembentukan kekayaan Bumiputera. Agihan dilaburkan semula secara automatik Sementara itu, Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif PHBAM, Zulkifli Ishak berkata pihaknya kekal komited menguruskan AHB secara bertanggungjawab supaya dana itu terus menjadi pilihan pelaburan yang mudah diakses oleh pelabur Bumiputera.

title: 'HLB Islamic fund lifts Langkawi entrepreneurs’ income
text:
'HLB Islamic fund lifts Langkawi entrepreneurs’ income

'KUALA LUMPUR: Aligned with its commitment to deepening its value-based intermediation (VBI) ecosystem, HLB Islamic has channeled RM138,600 in social financing towards social enterprise SURI Inspirasi under Bank Negara Malaysia’s (BNM) iTEKAD framework, which has led to a 94% average surge in monthly income and over RM14,000 in total new earnings for participating entrepreneurs of SURI’s Sustainable Reliable Income (SRI) programme. The SRI programme empowers underserved communities to upcycle discarded fabrics into unique fashion items, creating sustainable jobs and encouraging entrepreneurship while promoting zero-waste fashion and community empowerment. As part of the programme, the participating entrepreneurs, predominantly underserved single mothers, produced 1,000 school uniforms for students across five schools in Langkawi, generating RM30,000 in savings for local families. HLB Islamic commemorated the milestone through the handover of high-grade sewing machines to the participating entrepreneurs, marking the transition from classroom learning to active enterprise ownership. According to HLBIslamic CEO Dafinah Ahmed Hilmi, “Our vision of financial stewardship is grounded in our Hayat @ HLB Islamic framework, which views wealth building as a purposeful journey across life stages, starting with wealth creation. Through our partnership with SURI, we are providing the community with the essential tools and training to unlock their entrepreneurial potential, and we hope this will catalyse a lifelong trajectory of building wealth towards financial independence that will enrich the community for generations to come.” This success marks a significant milestone in HLB Islamic’s ongoing collaboration with SURI, who first entered the bank’s ecosystem as a participant of the HLB Jumpstart initiative. Launched to incubate high-impact Malaysian social enterprises through commercial mentorship, branding, and digital capacity building, HLB Jumpstart provided SURI with the early framework to scale its operations, illustrating the bank’s long-term strategy of nurturing social ventures into self-sustaining implementation partners capable of delivering widespread impact.

title: 'Stock Focus
text:
'Stock Focus

'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL: CIMB) could potentially raise its RM2 billion capital return commitment to increase the chances of its share buyback programme garnering investor acceptance, according to MBSB Research.  A higher capital-return commitment could help offset potential disappointment among investors who are expecting a larger portion of the RM2 billion to be returned via special dividends, the research house said.  “To increase its chances of success, we think there is a likelihood of CIMB positively revising to the RM2.0 billion figure, and that CIMB is confident enough on its ability to garner sufficient capital before signalling to the market via share buybacks,” MBSB Research said in a note on Thursday.  “We would not put it past CIMB’s management to pull off such a manoeuvre — they’ve surprised us positively multiple times in the past,” it added.  MBSB Research noted that share buybacks have historically not been successful in Malaysia. CIMB’s share buybacks make up a portion of its RM2 billion capital return scheme, of which RM700 million has already been returned via special dividends.  The primary purpose of the share buybacks is for CIMB to further drive its earnings per share, return on equity (ROE) and dividend per share figures, MBSB Research noted, particularly as the bank is slightly behind on its ROE target for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026 (FY2026).  The research house noted CIMB has been buying back shares every day, tallying up to 20.76 million shares for RM163 million since Sept 21 thus far.  Who could follow CIMB?  CIMB’s share buyback programme is also being watched for its potential implications on other banks, according to MBSB Research.  The research house described the programme as the first major share buyback scheme by a Malaysian bank for capital management purposes in many years, and said a successful outcome could encourage other large banks to consider similar measures.  It listed Public Bank Bhd (KL: PBBANK) and RHB Bank Bhd (KL: RHBBANK) as possible candidates.  Public Bank, it noted, has already received shareholder approval for a share buyback of up to 10% of its shares, although it has not done any yet. Its management has maintained that this is a capital optimisation option rather than a set path they want to go down, the research house added.  RHB Bank, meanwhile, has high capital ratios and historically releases excess capital via larger payouts in the fourth quarter, MBSB Research noted. It is currently preparing a new capital release plan, which is scheduled to be announced by the first quarter of FY2027, the research house added.  MBSB Research maintained its “buy” call on CIMB but with a lower target price of RM9.20 from RM9.29, based on an unchanged FY2027 forecast price-to-book value of 1.33 times.  At the time of writing, shares of CIMB were down three sen or 0.39% at RM7.76, valuing the lender at RM84 billion.

title: 'Maybank falls below RM10 for first time in nine months, rising bond yields hurt banking stocks
text:
'Maybank falls below RM10 for first time in nine months, rising bond yields hurt banking stocks

'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK) fell below RM10 for the first time in nearly nine months and banking stocks mostly declined on Thursday amid rising bond yields. Higher yields generally hurt banks as they take larger paper losses from lower prices of the bonds they hold, which eats into capital and forces them to book losses if they sell. Banks will also have to increase their rates to attract depositors, leading to higher funding costs. That would weigh on banks’ near term non-interest income as well as their capital ratios, Affin Hwang Investment Bank flagged in a note on Thursday. Maybank, the country’s top bank in terms of assets, fell for the third straight day and closed down 0.4% at RM9.95. CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) and Hong Leong Bank Bhd (KL:HLBANK) each declined over 1%. The Bursa Malaysia Financial Services Index, which also tracks non-bank firms such as insurers and stockbrokers, fell to its lowest level in 10 months. The US Federal Reserve raised interest rates earlier this month for the first time in three years, sending the yield on the 10-year benchmark Malaysian Government Securities to as high as 4.18% before moderating. A growing number of economists expect Bank Negara Malaysia to raise the overnight policy rate in November during the final scheduled monetary policy review for the year. Rising yields tend to lead to higher corporate bond yields, which also tie-in to capital raising decisions both for banks and other corporates and, subsequently, fee income to the banks, Affin Hwang said. Maybank and Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd (KL:ABMB) have on their books the longest bond duration — the length of time for a bond to repay its cost in cash flows while also being a measure of sensitivity to changes in interest rates — according to the research house’s analysis. Public Bank Bhd (KL:PBBANK) and Hong Leong Bank, meanwhile, have the shortest duration. In terms of capital ratios, Maybank, RHB Bank Bhd (KL:RHBBANK) and CIMB could see the largest drops, while Public Bank and Hong Leong Bank would see the least due to their portfolios’ shorter duration, the house added.

title: 'From F1 to the World Cup: How Anwar is using sport as diplomacy to put Malaysia on the world stage
text:
'From F1 to the World Cup: How Anwar is using sport as diplomacy to put Malaysia on the world stage

'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s approach of leveraging sports as a platform for diplomacy, economic activity and nation branding is helping position Malaysia back on the global sporting stage, according to an analyst. Global Peace Institute, London senior fellow Prof Dr Mohd Mizan Mohammad Aslam said Malaysia had, in recent months, demonstrated how global sporting events could be used not only to entertain the public but also to strengthen international relationships, generate economic activity and create a sense of shared national excitement. “Sport is often treated as entertainment, but for governments it can also be diplomacy, economic policy and nation branding rolled into one,” he said in a statement today. Formula 1’s return to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) after nine years and Malaysia’s efforts to ensure access to the 2026 Fifa World Cup broadcasts demonstrated how sports could be used to strengthen the country’s international engagement. Mohd Mizan said Malaysia’s hosting of the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix from Oct 2–4 demonstrated the international dimension of sports diplomacy, after the Bahrain Grand Prix could not proceed at its original venue due to geopolitical conditions in West Asia. He said the arrangement went beyond a commercial transaction involving a racetrack, as it was facilitated within the wider relationship between Malaysia and Bahrain, with the support of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and Bahrain’s King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa. Bahrain’s Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa also travelled to Malaysia and met Anwar during the race weekend. Mohd Mizan said Anwar’s attendance at the qualifying session at Sepang, visit to the Mercedes-AMG Petronas pit and participation in a reception hosted by Prince Salman further demonstrated how the sporting event created a platform for diplomatic engagement. “Sport had therefore created a diplomatic platform. Leaders met, bilateral relations were reinforced and Malaysia was placed before a global audience not through a formal summit but through one of the world’s most recognisable sporting spectacles,” he said. Mohd Mizan said the public response to F1’s return was equally significant, with around 95,000 three-day tickets sold by late September and SIC expecting sales to reach about 100,000, which would be the highest ticket sales recorded for races held at the circuit. He said the event also generated significant economic spillovers, with the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture estimating that it could draw around 300,000 tourists, including about 50,000 international visitors, while Hong Leong Bank Research projected an economic impact of approximately RM1.3 billion through sports tourism and foreign visitor spending. “Formula 1 does not benefit only the circuit.

title: 'Pelabur asing jual RM799.9 juta ekuiti Bursa Malaysia untuk minggu kedua - MBSB Research - Newswav
text:
'Pelabur asing jual RM799.9 juta ekuiti Bursa Malaysia untuk minggu kedua - MBSB Research - Newswav

'KUALA LUMPUR 5 Okt – Pelabur asing terus mengurangkan pegangan dalam pasaran saham Malaysia apabila mencatatkan jualan bersih RM799.9 juta bagi minggu berakhir 2 Oktober 2026, menurut MBSB Research. Jualan bersih itu menjadikan aliran keluar dana asing di Bursa Malaysia berterusan untuk minggu kedua berturut-turut dengan pelabur asing menjadi penjual bersih pada kesemua lima hari dagangan sepanjang minggu berkenaan. “Jualan paling tinggi direkodkan pada Rabu sebanyak RM228.4 juta, diikuti Khamis RM187.9 juta, Selasa RM172.4 juta, Isnin RM142.1 juta dan Jumaat RM69.1 juta,” kata MBSB Research dalam nota kajiannya. Pelabur tempatan ambil peluang Berbeza dengan pelabur asing, institusi tempatan meneruskan trend pembelian bersih untuk minggu kedua berturut-turut dengan aliran masuk RM352.4 juta. Pelabur runcit pula meneruskan pembelian bersih bagi minggu keenam berturut-turut dengan jumlah aliran masuk sebanyak RM447.5 juta. Ini menunjukkan tekanan jualan daripada pelabur asing sebahagiannya diimbangi oleh penyertaan pelabur tempatan. Dari segi aktiviti dagangan, purata dagangan harian pelabur runcit meningkat 3.7%, manakala institusi tempatan susut 7.9%. Penyertaan pelabur asing pula meningkat 8.6%. title: 'Maybank Turned Its Cash Back Card Perks Into A Playground At Mid Valley
text:
'Maybank Turned Its Cash Back Card Perks Into A Playground At Mid Valley

'Last week, we dropped by Mid Valley Megamall to check out the Maybank Cash Back Mastercard Platinum showcase. Held at Centre Court from 23 to 27 September, the five-day event had a little bit of everything, from interactive activities to a closer look at the card’s features.  A Station For The Card’s Benefits  The showcase was set up like a stamp-card journey. We picked up a journey card at the start and worked our way through five stations. The first four were More To Discover, Stream For More, More To Enjoy and More To Unwind. Once we had collected all four stamps, we could head to the final stop, Maybank Cafe, and redeem either a ZUS Coffee or a Krispy Kreme doughnut.  The activities at each station were also designed around the card’s benefits. One had a touchscreen game where you had to catch groceries in a basket, a playful take on the card’s 8% cash back on digital lifestyle spending. There were also photo spots with airplane window backdrops featuring destinations like Singapore, Thailand, Japan and South Korea, which are among the countries where the card charges no foreign exchange mark-up fee.  Visitors who applied for the card on-site could unlock three additional activities. These included a Flight Simulator and a Merchandise Redemption station with goodies such as a Maybank tumbler and Lilo & Stitch tote bag. Applicants could also try their luck at a giant Gashapon machine for prizes including a Nintendo Switch 2, Setel vouchers and Grab vouchers.  Card Benefits At A Glance  The Event Has Ended, But You Can Still Win  If you missed the showcase, you can still catch Maybank’s upcoming contest for cardholders, which runs from 1 October to 31 December 2026.  You’ll earn entries by spending at least RM1,000 a month on the card, giving you a chance to win one of these prizes:  Full contest details are available on Maybank’s contest page. title: 'CIMB Bank wins big at Euromoney Awards
text:
'CIMB Bank wins big at Euromoney Awards

'PETALING JAYA: CIMB Bank Bhd and CIMB Investment Bank have won top accolades at the Euromoney Awards for Excellence 2026, taking home top honours as Malaysia’s Best Retail Bank, Malaysia’s Best Digital Bank for SMEs, and Malaysia’s Best Investment Bank. The bank said in a statement that the awards reflected the ongoing focus on providing customer-centric solutions through innovation, digital capabilities and deep market expertise across its retail, small and medium enterprise (SME), and investment banking businesses. CIMB Group Holdings Bhd group chief executive officer Novan Amirudin commented that the recognitions are a testament to the trust of the group’s customers and the dedication of its teams. “They reaffirm CIMB’s purpose of advancing customers and society by making financial solutions more accessible, relevant and impactful for the people and businesses we serve,” he added. “As their needs continue to evolve, we remain committed to being a trusted partner supporting individuals in realising their aspirations and helping businesses achieve their growth ambitions through meaningful and lasting value creation.” CIMB’s latest wins come amid the bank’s continued efforts to empower customers through accessible, inclusive and purpose-driven financial solutions. In retail banking, it has been working to deepen its franchise through personalisation offerings, digitally enabled journeys, and stronger engagement across segments. The bank said revenue and profitability had advanced during the year, underpinned by market share gains in auto finance, credit cards and retail deposits, on top of progress in digital sales and customer cross-sell. It also continued to strengthen wealth proposition through differentiated investment solutions, broader product diversity, chief investment office-led advisory capabilities and enhanced digital wealth platform, with particular momentum seen in the “Preferred” affluent segment as it expands its advisory-led and relationship-based wealth capabilities. Meanwhile, the bank has continued to advance its SME services, having launched the CIMB OCTO Biz digital banking platform, which has amassed more than 280,000 customers to date. Additionally, it has expanded financing access through embedded merchant financing with TNG eWallet and its flexible financing through its SME FlexiCash. Beyond this, CIMB Investment Bank in 2025 secured the top ranking in Malaysian equity and debt capital markets by deal value and share of wallet, as well as the highest position in Asean equity and debt capital markets by deal value, cementing its position both locally and regionally.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia ends lower, KLCI slides 1.26pc on cautious sentiment
text:
'Bursa Malaysia ends lower, KLCI slides 1.26pc on cautious sentiment

'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Bursa Malaysia ended lower on Thursday amid continued selling pressure, tracking a mixed and cautious Wall Street performance overnight. At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) fell 20.81 points, or 1.26 per cent, to 1,630.36 from Wednesday’s close of 1,651.17. The benchmark index, which opened 1.30 points weaker at 1,649.87, moved between 1,630.10 and 1,649.87 throughout the trading session. Market breadth was also negative, with decliners outpacing gainers 750 to 342, while 495 counters were unchanged, 1,186 untraded and 12 suspended. Turnover fell to 3.1 billion units, worth RM2.7 billion, from 3.63 billion units valued at RM3.62 billion on Wednesday. IPPFA Sdn Bhd director of investment strategy and country economist Mohd Sedek Jantan said sentiment was cautious, reinforced by weaker domestic manufacturing activity and continued foreign selling. He said softer manufacturing momentum and portfolio rotation in global markets kept the benchmark index under pressure, with domestic institutional demand remaining an important counterbalance to persistent foreign outflows. Earlier, the S&P Global Malaysia Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) edged slightly below the neutral 50.0 mark, falling to 49.9 in September from 50.2 in August, marking the first decline in four months after a sustained period of improvement. Regionally, the S&P Global ASEAN Manufacturing PMI fell to 52.1 in September from 52.3 in August. Among the heavyweight counters, Maybank fell four sen to RM9.95, while Public Bank lost three sen to RM4.67, and CIMB dropped 10 sen to RM7.69. Tenaga Nasional declined six sen to RM12.90, and IHH Healthcare erased 13 sen to RM7.70. In active trade, Zetrix AI firmed half a sen to 16.5 sen, VS Industry dipped one sen to 27 sen, and Jaks Resources slipped 2.5 sen to 18 sen. title: 'Govt Dividend Receipts Up 1.4% to RM39.55b in 2025 on Higher BNM, Khazanah Payouts — AG’s Report
text:
'Govt Dividend Receipts Up 1.4% to RM39.55b in 2025 on Higher BNM, Khazanah Payouts — AG’s Report

'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): The federal government received RM39.55 billion in dividends from its investments in 2025, up by 1.4% from RM39.01 billion a year earlier, as higher payouts from Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and Khazanah Nasional Bhd outweighed lower receipts from other entities. The dividends came from 20 companies and two statutory bodies, compared with 21 companies and two statutory bodies in 2024. The increase was RM535.06 million compared to last year, according to the latest auditor general’s report released on Monday. Petroliam Nasional Bhd (PETRONAS) paid RM32 billion, unchanged from 2024. BNM paid RM5.25 billion, up from RM2.85 billion, an increase of RM2.4 billion or 84.2%. Khazanah's dividend doubled to RM2 billion from RM1 billion. Bank Simpanan Nasional paid RM25 million, down from RM52 million. Dividends from statutory bodies rose 81.8% to RM5.28 billion, while those from companies fell 5.1% to RM34.27 billion. In all, nine companies and one statutory body paid RM7.43 billion, against RM3.98 billion in 2024, an increase of RM3.45 billion or 86.7%. Twelve companies and one statutory body paid less compared to 2024, as three companies paid the same amount in both years. Piramid Pertama Sdn Bhd, which paid RM2.73 billion in 2024, made no payment in 2025. Dividends from Prokhas Sdn Bhd fell to RM5.6 million from RM56.24 million. Three companies, Perbadanan Nasional Bhd, Malaysia Debt Ventures Bhd and Malaysia Digital Economy Corp Sdn Bhd paid dividends in 2025 after paying none in 2024. Source: TheEdge - 6 Oct 2026

title: 'Anak syarikat ES Sunlogy tuntut RM1.17 juta daripada Ecolectric, Maybank terlibat prosiding garnisi - Newswav
text:
'Anak syarikat ES Sunlogy tuntut RM1.17 juta daripada Ecolectric, Maybank terlibat prosiding garnisi - Newswav

'KUALA LUMPUR 2 Okt - Anak syarikat milik penuh ES Sunlogy Berhad, Savelite Engineering Sdn Bhd sedang mengambil tindakan untuk menguatkuasakan penghakiman mahkamah bernilai RM1.17 juta terhadap Ecolectric Engineering Sdn Bhd selepas Mahkamah Tinggi membenarkan prosiding garnisi melibatkan Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank). Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Lumpur membenarkan permohonan Savelite bagi Perintah Garnisi Tunjuk Sebab terhadap Maybank, yang dinamakan sebagai garnisi pertama Ecolectric, dalam pendengaran ex parte pada 30 September lalu, menurut pemakluman ES Sunlogy kepada Bursa Malaysia. Mahkamah menetapkan 21 Oktober 2026 bagi pendengaran tunjuk sebab. Perintah Garnisi atau Garnishee Order merupakan proses undang-undang yang membolehkan pihak yang memperoleh penghakiman mahkamah memohon mendapatkan bayaran daripada wang milik pihak yang berhutang di bawah penghakiman tetapi dipegang oleh pihak ketiga, seperti bank. Dalam kes ini, Maybank dinamakan sebagai garnisi dan perlu menunjukkan sebab kepada mahkamah sebelum mahkamah memutuskan sama ada wang yang mungkin dipegang bagi pihak Ecolectric boleh digunakan untuk memenuhi penghakiman tersebut. Savelite akan mendapatkan Perintah Garnisi Tunjuk Sebab itu dan mengatur penyerahannya kepada Maybank mengikut arahan mahkamah. Prosiding itu menyusuli penghakiman ingkar pembelaan yang direkodkan terhadap Ecolectric pada 17 Ogos 2026 berhubung pertikaian kerja pemasangan elektrik bagi projek pembangunan kediaman di Damansara Heights. Pertikaian projek Damansara Heights Menerusi penghakiman itu, Ecolectric diperintahkan membayar RM1,174,327.72 kepada Savelite dalam tempoh 14 hari. Jumlah itu merupakan RM1,234,551.27 yang diputuskan mahkamah selepas ditolak wang tahanan RM60,223.55 yang dipegang Savelite. Pertikaian itu berpunca daripada surat anugerah bernilai kira-kira RM1.65 juta bertarikh 25 April 2022, apabila Savelite melantik Ecolectric sebagai subkontraktor untuk membekalkan tenaga kerja bagi pemasangan perkhidmatan elektrik untuk projek pembangunan kediaman 54 unit di Damansara Heights. Savelite mendakwa Ecolectric gagal atau enggan menempatkan tenaga kerja yang mencukupi atau berkemahiran di tapak, menyebabkan kerja tidak dapat dilaksanakan mengikut program yang dipersetujui. Savelite memfailkan writ saman dan penyata tuntutan terhadap Ecolectric pada Julai 2026. Menurut pemakluman ES Sunlogy, Ecolectric tidak memasukkan kehadiran dalam tempoh 14 hari selepas writ saman dan penyata tuntutan diserahkan serta gagal memfail dan menyerahkan pembelaannya dalam tempoh ditetapkan. Mahkamah Tinggi kemudian merekodkan penghakiman ingkar pembelaan terhadap Ecolectric pada 17 Ogos 2026. Selain bayaran RM1.17 juta, mahkamah memerintahkan ganti rugi am ditaksir dan kos RM528 dibayar oleh Ecolectric kepada Savelite. ES Sunlogy sebelum ini berkata Savelite telah membuat rosot nilai penuh sebanyak RM3.

title: 'Aktiviti buru saham pacu Bursa Malaysia ditutup tinggi, sentimen positif
text:
'Aktiviti buru saham pacu Bursa Malaysia ditutup tinggi, sentimen positif

'Bursa Malaysia meningkat selepas mengalami pemulihan kecil pada akhir dagangan Jumaat, dipacu oleh aktiviti memburu saham-saham berharga rendah susulan jualan ketara baru-baru ini, kata penganalisis.  Lantunan itu bagaimanapun kekurangan momentum ketika pasaran Asia kekal diasak tekanan menjelang pengumuman data pasaran tenaga kerja Amerika Syarikat (AS).  Pada 5 petang, indeks penunjuk utama FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) menokok 0.51 mata atau 0.03 peratus kepada 1,630.87 daripada paras penutup 1,630.36, semalam.  Indeks penanda aras itu yang dibuka menokok 3.51 mata kepada 1,633.87, bergerak dalam jajaran 1,630.63 hingga 1,640.78 sepanjang sesi dagangan.  Sentimen pasaran positif dengan kaunter untung mengatasi rugi iaitu 585 berbanding 541 manakala 558 lain tidak berubah, 1,089 tidak diniagakan dan 24 lain digantung dagangannya.  Jumlah dagangan meningkat kepada 4.23 bilion unit bernilai RM2.70 bilion daripada 3.1 bilion unit bernilai RM2.7 bilion, semalam.  Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd Thong Pak Leng berkata aktiviti penjualan pada baru-baru ini menyaksikan penilaian saham mewah yang lebih menarik, sekali gus berpotensi menggalakkan usaha pengumpulan saham secara berperingkat.  Namun pada masa sama, katanya, pelabur terus mengambil langkah untuk kekal bertahan berikutan perkembangan seperti hasil bon dan harga minyak mentah yang kekal tinggi.  “Bagi bursa tempatan pula, kami berpendirian berhati-hati di disebalik peningkatan berikutan risiko cabaran luar yang mungkin mengekalkan ketidaktentuan pasaran pada tahap tinggi,” katanya kepada Bernama.  Saham wajaran tinggi menyaksikan Maybank naik tujuh sen kepada RM10.02, Public Bank susut satu sen kepada RM4.66, CIMB berkurangan empat sen kepada RM7.65, Tenaga Nasional meningkat enam sen kepada RM12.96 dan IHH Healthcare meraih 10 sen kepada RM7.80.  Saham paling aktif menyaksikan Zetrix AI susut lima sen kepada 11.5 sen, Jaks Resources tidak berubah pada 18 sen, JCY International menokok 10.5 sen kepada 66 sen, V.S Industry naik dua sen kepada 29 sen dan PUC menambah satu sen kepada 4.5 sen.  Bagi saham paling untung, Malaysian Pacific Industries melonjak RM1.28 kepada RM42.40, UWC naik 47 sen kepada RM7.57, Vitrox menokok 46 sen kepada RM10.46, United Plantations meraih 42 sen kepada RM31.38 manakala UMS Integration meningkat 38 sen kepada RM9.03.  Saham yang mencatatkan penurunan ketara diterajui oleh Nestle yang susut 48 sen kepada RM89.52, Kuala Lumpur Kepong turun 42 sen kepada RM21, Enra berkurangan 25.5 sen kepada 72.5 sen manakala Allianz Malaysia dan Hong Leong Bank masing-masing menguncup 20 sen kepada RM20.80 dan RM22.64.  Di papan indeks pula, Indeks FBM Mid 70 meningkat 122.94 mata kepada 17,481.93, Indeks FBM Emas menokok 27.04 mata kepada 12,170.57 manakala Indeks FBM Top 100 naik 24.52 mata kepada 11,957.68.  Indeks FBM Emas Syariah meningkat 47.31 mata kepada 12,060.

title: 'Maybank, ABS jalin kerjasama tingkat piawaian penasihat kekayaan
text:
'Maybank, ABS jalin kerjasama tingkat piawaian penasihat kekayaan

'PETALING JAYA: Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank) dan Asian Banking School (ABS) menandatangani Memorandum Persefahaman (MoU) bagi membangunkan kerangka pensijilan profesional penasihat kekayaan pertama yang diiktiraf industri di Malaysia. Kerangka kerja yang dikenali sebagai Program Pensijilan Pengurusan dan Penasihat Kekayaan ABS itu bertujuan menetapkan standard kompetensi khusus bagi profesional penasihat kekayaan dalam sektor perbankan. Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif Kumpulan Perkhidmatan Kewangan Komuniti Maybank, Syed Ahmad Taufik Albar berkata, kerjasama itu membolehkan Maybank menyumbang pengalaman melangkaui organisasi bagi meningkatkan standard profesional di Malaysia. “Maybank terus melabur dalam membangunkan profesional kekayaan kami menerusi Maybank Wealth Academy bagi membina keupayaan penasihatan holistik yang memenuhi keperluan kewangan pelanggan. “Peluang ini turut membuka ruang untuk memeluaskan elemen program berkenaan ke peringkat serantau dari semasa ke semasa,” katanya dalam kenyataan. Sementara itu, Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif ABS, Profesor Dr. Manivanan Saman berkata, gabungan kepakaran ABS dan pengalaman praktikal Maybank bertujuan mewujudkan laluan kredibel yang memberikan penanda aras lebih jelas kepada profesional kekayaan. “Maybank bertindak sebagai Rakan Industri Pengasas dengan menyumbang kepakaran dan pengalaman dalam pembangunan bakat, manakala ABS membawa kepakaran dalam pembangunan dan pensijilan perbankan profesional,” katanya. Pengambilan pertama bagi program berkenaan dijangka bermula pada separuh kedua tahun 2027, dengan Maybank berhasrat mengintegrasikannya ke dalam Maybank Wealth Academy. Langkah berkenaan memperkukuh francais pengurusan kekayaan Maybank yang baru-baru ini dinamakan sebagai Bank Swasta Terbaik Malaysia 2026 oleh Euromoney serta Bank Pengurusan Kekayaan Terbaik di Malaysia oleh Alpha Southeast Asia bagi tahun ke-10 berturut-turut. –UTUSAN

title: '石隆门女子遭假贷款群组连环套 汇款3次始觉受骗向警方求助
text:
'石隆门女子遭假贷款群组连环套 汇款3次始觉受骗向警方求助

'（古晋3日讯）意图通过网上个人贷款缓解经济，学校保洁掉入网上诈骗陷阱，3次汇款共6400令吉给老千后，老千继续各种理由要求汇款、保洁才如梦初醒被骗并来到石隆门警局报案求助。  上述欺骗案是发生在石隆门警区，受害者是现年40岁来自石隆门甘榜瑟吉邦的女子，在石隆门某间政中任职保洁工作。  受害者是昨午5时15分来到石隆门警局报案求助，商业犯罪调查查案官已着手展开调查工作。  石隆门警区主任莫哈默海德今早向媒体发布有关讯息。  受害者是在9月28在工作地点游览面子书时，看到名为“myringgitcash”的个人贷款广告，并有意申请1万令吉的个人贷款。  受害人点击广告链接填写了申请人的个人信息，随后被添加到一个名为“myringgit10k”的WhatsApp群组。  加入该WhatsApp群组后，受害人与3名自称是群组管理员的人员联系，联系电话号码分别为011-11236641、011-21097126和011-28589136。  在与3个人交涉后，受害人于 9 月 29 日通过“myringgit10k”WhatsApp 群组被告知，其申请的贷款已获批准，并要求投诉人预先支付几笔款项，据称是为了将贷款资金存入受害人的账户。  因此，投诉人向2个不同的账户进行了三笔交易，具体如下：  2026年9月30日，向Muhammad Nurzaidi Bin Nazri名下的Maybank账户（151342200688）汇款1,100.00令吉 2026年10月1日，向Kannan A/L Gagendran名下的Maybank账户（362405001788）汇款2,200.00令吉 2026年10月1日，向Kannan A/L Gagendran名下的Maybank账户（362405001788）汇款3,140.00令吉  付款后，受害人仍被要求支付额外款项，但由于他认为自己受到了欺骗且未收到任何款项，因此没有继续支付并火速来道警局报案求助。
